items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: It brings to mind right there a very funny story about Chink Morton, the old bass player.

ctx.x: Yeah. Oh. Of course, it was very simple for him to take it and put it on the cornet once he, once he, once he, he worked it out on piano. Mm. You see, because he, his harmonies, he relied on his harmonies so much. That's what he told me. His changes, his chord progressions. Mm-hmm. It brings to mind right there a very funny story about Chink Morton, the old bass player. Mm-hmm. Who is 88 years old today. He played, he played with, with the Red Dead Kings for a while.
And he told me when they were at Fry's Inn in Chicago that Bix used to come around there.

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: And then playing around the spots, being associated with fellows like Chink Morton, old timers like that. They really helped to a great extent.

ctx.x: Kind of like a Wausau just played for fun. They just go around and listen and pick up things. That's right.

I would say my association with Buzzy Williams was really great. And then playing around the spots, being associated with fellows like Chink Morton, old timers like that. They really helped to a great extent. Harry Shields. I met Leon Rapolo one time when I was at the Valencia. And he sat in and played. But he just played a few tunes and that was all.
Was he playing good then? He was playing real good then.
